reasons: Direction is correctly identified: § 7.2 imposes the MFN obligation on Customer (must disclose and match any more favourable third-party offer for Vendor's benefit), which is the burdening direction the rule targets; no Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial is lost.
The redline achieves the preferred position with the minimal edit — full deletion of the single-sentence obligation — and no collateral changes were made to other paragraphs.

The comment is accurate and appropriately toned: it states what was deleted, why (reverse MFN, conflict with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in § 12.3), and offers the playbook fallback (single defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs).
Deterministic check confirms the operation applies; the high changed-character ratio inherent in a deletion is justified because the rule's remedy is to delete the obligation.
